messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: HIGH - customer OrchidLabs (private VPC) seeing widespread 5xx on /v1/generate via private NLB. 504/502 spikes since 09:41 UTC. Paging @eve (oncall) and neteng.

eve (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. @maya can you grab NLB health and ALB/NAT stats? I'll start collecting early impact.

maya (sre): Pulling metrics now. Cloudwatch shows NLB target_healthy_count dropping to 0 for orchid-prod-nlb at 09:40. Target group still has targets in service but healthcheck failing: "HTTP 503" from backend.

nitin (neteng): Any recent SG changes or route updates for this tenant? Orchid is on private deployment in eqx-1, dedicated pool 4.

alison (solutions): I just spoke to their on-call (J. Park) — they're seeing timeouts from their side to our NLB IPs, started ~09:39. No config changes on their side per them.

maya (sre): Checking recent deploys... ops-bot shows a control-plane config push at 09:35 that touched NAT gateway scaling for eqx-1 (rollback candidate). Investigating correlation.

ops-bot: Deploy: infra/controlplane@c3f2 - autoscale natgw pools (eqx-1) - started 09:35 - status: success.

eve (oncall): Ok. Two parallel hypotheses: (1) backend hosts rejecting healthchecks (app issue) (2) NLB->backend connectivity problem, maybe SG/conntrack or NAT exhaustion. Nitin, can you confirm SG rules for NLB -> backend? Also need per-tenant conntrack counts.

nitin (neteng): SGs unchanged since yesterday. I'll run a quick connectivity probe from our pinger host into the backend subnet and check conntrack on the NAT instances.

maya (sre): Running a curl against target healthcheck path from inside VPC:

```
curl -v --max-time 5 http://10.10.45.12:8080/health
*   Trying 10.10.45.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 10.10.45.12 (10.10.45.12) port 8080 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 10.10.45.12:8080\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable\nDate: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 09:42:18 GMT\nContent-Type: application/json\nContent-Length: 48\n\n{"uptime":12345,"status":"degraded","reason":"overload"}
```

maya (sre): Backend returns 503 with body "reason":"overload". Not pure network blackhole.

eve (oncall): That points to app overload or resource starvation on the nodes serving Orchid. Check per-host CPU, disk, and open file descriptors.

nitin (neteng): Conntrack on natgw-01: entries 79k / limit 80k — really close. natgw-02: 32k. Traffic skewed to natgw-01. Could be asymmetric routing + NAT exhaustion causing partial failures.

alison (solutions): Orchid has sticky routing to natgw-01 via route table - is that expected? Their tenancy config pinned them for compliance.

eve (oncall): If natgw-01 is near exhaustion, healthchecks might intermittently fail causing NLB to mark targets unhealthy. Immediate mitigation: shift Orchid traffic away from natgw-01 by updating route table to natgw-02 (quick partial failover) and reduce per-tenant flow by placing a temporary rate-limit at the NLB ALB edge. Kevin please notify customer about short outage and our mitigation plan.

kevin (acct): I'll call J. Park and let them know we're shifting routing and doing a brief maintenance window. ETA 10 minutes.

nitin (neteng): Making route change now: modifying rt-orchid-prod to point to natgw-02. Pushing... done at 09:50.

ops-bot: Route update: rt-orchid-prod -> natgw-02 by nitin at 09:50 UTC.

maya (sre): Watching conntrack after change. natgw-01 reduced to 40k entries in 30s; natgw-02 now 58k. NLB target_healthy_count rising back to expected at 09:51.

eve (oncall): Rolling healthcheck pass observed. ALB traffic back to normal latencies ~120ms, 502s dropping. Marking mitigation as effective for now. Keeping on-call engaged while we stabilize.

alison (solutions): Customer confirmed transient errors cleared after ~09:52. They saw brief spike in errors for ~12 minutes. They reported no config changes.

maya (sre): Root cause hypothesis: control-plane autoscale shift caused disproportionate SNAT usage to natgw-01, combined with tenant stickiness and app threads hitting resource limits -> backend returned 503 under load -> NLB flapped targets.

eve (oncall): Immediate next steps (in-thread):
- Keep traffic routed to natgw-02 for 1h and monitor (maya)
- Add temporary NLB rate-limiter on orchid route to mitigate bursty flows (nitin)
- Rotate backend instances one-at-a-time with lower concurrency to relieve app overload (maya)
- Open RFC ticket to remove single-natgw pinning for tenants and add autoscaling distribution (infra)
- Notify customer via email with incident summary and ETA for postmortem (kevin)

nitin (neteng): Applying rate-limit ACL on orchid-nlb: limit 2000cps -> applied at 09:54.

ops-bot: Rate-limit ACL applied to orchid-nlb by nitin - ACL ID acl-ork-2000 - 09:54 UTC.

maya (sre): Starting staggered rolling restart of orchard-backend-asg: will cycle 2 at a time to avoid cold starts. First batch started 09:58.

eve (oncall): Monitoring. If errors reappear, we'll rollback route and re-evaluate. Also prepare a fallback: shift Orchid to dedicated fallback pool 7 if instability persists.

alison (solutions): I'll prepare a customer-facing blameless note and set expectation for a postmortem. Will coordinate time with Orchid's SREs.

kevin (acct): Called customer, left message while they were on a call; they replied via email and asked for a short incident summary. I'll send once we have initial impact numbers.

maya (sre): Current impact: total 5xx count peaked at ~9.8k errors between 09:39-09:51 for Orchid. Error window ~12 minutes. No other tenants affected.

eve (oncall): Good containment. Marking this P1 -> active mitigation. Oncall will remain until 12:00 UTC for stability checks. Will open INCIDENT ticket in tracker and add timeline.

ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-5723 by eve - severity P1 - OrchidLabs private VPC ingress/egress - 09:41 UTC.

eve (oncall): Postmortem action items (assignments):
- nitin: remove tenant pinning and implement natgw distribution (infra/2w)
- maya: improve backend autoscaling triggers to avoid overload on cold nodes (sre/1w)
- alison: customer comms & postmortem draft (comms/48h)
- ops: add alert for conntrack > 70% per natgw (infra/1d)

maya (sre): Logs and excerpts saved to incident bucket: s3://incidents/2026/INC-5723/logs. Will attach to ticket.

eve (oncall): Thanks team. Closing thread for now — will post final update after 1h monitoring or earlier if anything changes. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Update: 10:35 UTC - metrics stable for 25m, 5xx at baseline. Leaving mitigation in place until change window.
